# Kyoto 3-Day Low-Walking Trip Plan

A relaxed Kyoto plan for **2 adults**, focused on temples, vegetarian-friendly food, and easy transit. I’ve kept each day balanced with **one indoor backup**, **minimal walking**, and only a few items that may need advance booking, clearly flagged.

# Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

## Day 1 — Higashiyama + Gion, Slow Start
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Kiyomizu-dera early, then a short taxi or bus hop to **Kodai-ji** for a calmer temple visit.
- **Afternoon:** Browse **Ninenzaka/Sannenzaka** at an easy pace, then rest at a café near Gion.
- **Dinner:** Vegetarian-friendly shojin ryori or tofu set meal in central Kyoto.
- **Indoor backup:** Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art or a tea house visit if weather turns.

## Day 2 — Arashiyama, Scenic but Gentle
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** **Tenryu-ji** garden and the bamboo grove; keep the route short and use the local train/taxi as needed.
- **Afternoon:** **Okochi Sanso Garden** if you want a quieter option, or skip to a riverside café and a boat ride only if energy is good.
- **Dinner:** Tofu cuisine or vegetarian ramen near central Kyoto on the return.
- **Indoor backup:** Kyoto Railway Museum or a covered market visit such as Nishiki Market for snacks and browsing.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Indoor backup:** Kyoto Railway Museum or a covered market visit such as Nishiki Market for snacks and browsing, Kyoto, Japan

## Day 3 — Northern Kyoto Temples + Market Food
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** **Kinkaku-ji** first, then a short transfer to **Ryoan-ji** for the rock garden.
- **Afternoon:** Return toward central Kyoto for **Nishiki Market** tasting stops and an easy dessert/café break.
- **Dinner:** Vegetarian izakaya-style meal or tofu hot pot to finish the trip.
- **Indoor backup:** Nishiki Market shopping arcades and nearby department store food halls are ideal if it rains.

# Budget Fit and Best Choices

| Day | Focus | Estimated Spend for 2 | Walking Load | Booking Risk |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Day 1 | Higashiyama temples + Gion | JPY 18,000–28,000 | Low to moderate | Low |
| Day 2 | Arashiyama gardens + café time | JPY 22,000–35,000 | Low | Low |
| Day 3 | Northern temples + market food | JPY 18,000–30,000 | Low | Low |
| Buffer | Transit, snacks, extras | JPY 15,000–25,000 | — | — |

**Budget check:** This plan should fit comfortably within **JPY 120,000 total** excluding flights, even with taxis for comfort and a few nicer meals.

**Best low-walking strategy**
- Use **taxis for short hops** between temple clusters.
- Stay in **central Kyoto or near Kyoto Station** for easier returns.
- Keep one major temple and one lighter stop per half-day.
- Build in café or market breaks between sights.

# Booking-Sensitive Stops to Flag

- **Tenryu-ji garden area:** usually easy to visit, but special events or seasonal crowding can change access.
- **Tea ceremony experiences:** often require advance booking if you want a specific time.
- **Popular kaiseki or shojin ryori restaurants:** reserve ahead if you want a top-rated place.
- **Kinkaku-ji / Kiyomizu-dera:** generally do not need advance booking for standard entry, but go early to avoid crowds.
